questions.label: Exercise 1
questions.prompt: Write a program that displays the message "Hello world!" using the print() function.
questions.scheme: Award 1 mark if the program displays the message "Hello world!" using the print function.

questions.label: Exercise 2
questions.prompt:
Write a program that will assign a name to a variable called 'name'. 
The program should then display a message greeting the person who's name you assigned.
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark if a name (any name) is assigned to a variable called 'name' - the value assigned should be a string.
Award 1 mark for correctly displaying a message with the name variable used in it.

questions.label: Exercise 3
questions.prompt:
Create a program that assigns your favourite class to a variable.  You can choose  the name of the variable.
The program should output the following message "My favourite class is "  following by your favourite class.
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for assigning a class (Computing, English, Maths, etc) to a variable - the value assigned should be a string, the name of the variable does not matter.  Keep in mind that the code has to run, so students shouldn't be using a variable name like 'class' as that is a keyword.
Award 1 mark for displaying the message "My favourite class is (favClass)" - favClass should be replaced by the class stored in the variable.
questions.example:
favClass = "Computing"
print("My favourite class is " + favClass)

questions.label: Exercise 4
questions.prompt:
Write a program that assigns your age to a variable called 'myAge'.   The value assigned should be an integer - no speech marks.
The program should then output a message telling the user how old you are.
questions.starter: #Hint: You will need to use the str() function.
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for correctly assigning an integer to a variable called 'myAge'.
Award 1 mark for using a print function to display a message containing this variable.
Award 1 mark for correct use of + and str(myAge) to concatenate and display the message.,
questions.example:
myAge=14
print("I am " + str(myAge) + " years old.")

questions.label: Exercise 5
questions.prompt:
Write a program that stores and displays the number of students in the class.
It should output the following message - "There are ... students in this class."
questions.starter: #Hint: Remember to use + in between any strings (or variables that use str()) that you want to join together.
questions.scheme:
Award 1 mark for correctly assigning an integer to a variable.
Award 1 mark for outputting the correct message ("There are ... students in this class")
Award 1 mark for correct use of str() and concatenation.
questions.example:
students = 20
print("There are " + str(students) + " students in this class.")
